data.name: Sinking Island
data.detailed_description:
Colocar já na lista de desejos


Acerca do jogo

From the creator of Syberia 1, Syberia 2, experience Benoit Sokal's fifth game.

At the base of a cliff on Sagorah Island, 82 year-old American billionaire Walter Jones is found dead next to his life's work; a massive Art Deco tower he had dreamed would become an elite getaway for international jet-setters. The only clues found at the scene include his wheelchair, abandoned at the edge of the cliff, and multiple scratches on his face. One of these scratches appears to have been made by a woman. Ten people were present on the island at the time of his death, among them the heirs to his vast fortune and legacy. Was his death an accident or murder?

Players assume the role of Jack Norm, a federal agent turned private dectective, who is taking a break in the atolls of the Indian Ocean when an old friend requests his assistance with the case. Jack has just three days to complete 10 gameplay missions, collecting valuable clues and storing evidence in his PPA (Personal Police Assistant). He will interrogate each of the 10 unusual suspects, using his keen deduction skills to determine who among them may have the most to gain from Walter Jones's death.

KEY POINTS:

  • An engaging and innovative game.
  • Choose between two styles of gameplay to carry out your quest: Time Mode or Adventure Mode
  • Another classic adventure game by French author Benoît Sokal
  • Interrogate each of the 10 unusual suspects, using your keen deduction skills to determine who among them may have the most to gain from Walter Jones's death.

data.short_description: Walter Jones, a billionaire had planned on opening up a resort for the rich and famous, but was killed before his dream could be achieved. It's up to Detective Jack Norm to crack the case by interviewing the people on Sinking Island to get valuable clues. A game from Benoit Sokal.

reviews.review:
A disaster of a point and click game that is filled with tedious repetition, timewasting, absurd pixel hunting, unclear gameflow, seemingly missing parts of the story and just straight up annoying moments.

The game routinely requires you to find tiny things that blend into the environment, sometimes going so far as to mark the majority of the clickable object in one zone and a small part secretly with another, smaller zone. Finding a dark object in a dark pile of trash in a dark room while the other part of that pile is also a much bigger clickable zone is one of such idiotic moments.

The game's novel mechanic is it asking you questions about the game and you needing to provide the evidence and clues to answer them. Unfortunately this system is complete ass. It usually asks you to fill 6-9 slots with information, and even if one is wrong, it will not accept it and will just say "nope it is wrong" without any indication as to which one is it.
It gives you clues that skip over the answer you're trying to answer, and while these clues CLEARLY answer the question, they are not eligible as the 'correct' answer just because they're used later. One egregious example was when the game asks you "who is a good shot?" and MULTIPLE people clearly answer "oh yeah this person is a very good shot" and none of these answers are considered correct because the game hates you.

The game has a lot of repeated voicelines and doesn't feature a decent mechanism of skipping them. You will often want to ask a question to all the people on the island, and the part of the playable character asking the question, which sometimes can be multiple sentences long, cannot be skipped without ALSO skipping the answer, which defeats the entire point. The interaction voicelines, however, cannot be skipped at all. Prepare to hear "Sorry I am distracted" a hundred times because that's what your character says when you've exhausted all the dialogue with a person for the moment.

What also bugged me was the characters- sure they're fine, but my god what on earth compelled the developers to make half of them generic white men wearing similar color jackets, and two of them even have a similar sounding first name to boot (Martin and Marco). No, them being similar is not relevant to the story. Without a nametag next to them I often mistook one for another.

The game wastes your time with lengthy traversal through mostly empty zones that cannot be skipped, only hurried by making your character run, but even then the transitions sometime take multiple seconds as your character slowly ascends the stairs or something.

I finished the game out of spite and by using a walkthrough by the end because these pixel hunting 'puzzles' and 'get 10/10 correct or you won't progress, tee-hee' are just an astonishingly shit game design.

Do not play this game without expecting to consult a walkthrough, because it will routinely stump you with situations that will make you say "well how the hell I should've found that?" many, many times. I suppose the mystery was fine, so if you want to just watch it for that, you might enjoy it somewhat.
